title: NDSU Report Estimates $14.9 Billion China Tariff Shortfall
description_short: A May 2026 NDSU report estimates China’s 2025/26 retaliatory tariffs cut U.S. agricultural exports to China by $14.9 billion annualized.
description_medium: North Dakota State University researchers’ May 2026 report estimates that China’s 2025/26 retaliatory tariffs reduced U.S. agricultural exports to China by $14.9 billion on an annualized basis over March 2025–February 2026. The model assigns about $6.8 billion to soybeans. The estimate measures China-bound export shortfall, not net losses to U.S. farmers; the report says some shipments were redirected to other markets.
description_long: North Dakota State University’s May 2026 Agricultural Trade Monitor assesses China’s 2025/26 retaliatory tariffs on U.S. agricultural exports. Its structural-gravity analysis estimates an annualized $14.9 billion shortfall in U.S. shipments to China during March 2025–February 2026, relative to a 2024 export baseline. The report attributes the estimate to the combined Fentanyl and Reciprocal tariff layers imposed since March 2025 and assigns about $6.8 billion of the modeled shortfall to soybeans. It says the model controls for supply and demand shocks, seasonality, and global commodity trends. The $14.9 billion is a China-specific export shortfall, not lost exports overall or net harm to farmers; some shipments went to other markets. The report’s recommended citation dates it May 20, 2026, correcting the frozen March 4, 2025 record date. The prior “72% soybean collapse” wording is also corrected: NDSU lists soybean exports falling from $12.6 billion in 2024 to $3.1 billion in 2025; 72% is the combined share of five commodity categories in the modeled shortfall.
